summary: Burns diesel with manifold oxygen inside a temperature-dependent air:fuel window; best efficiency near ratio 13.6 cold and 14.0 hot, no fuel above 60 RPS.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: A cylinder produces torque only when the crank is above 2 RPS, its air:fuel ratio is inside the window 12 − 2t … 16 + 4t (t = manifold °C ÷ 100, clamped 0…1), and the crank is at or below 60 RPS. Fuel is capped by the diesel available in its fuel manifolds and intake by the oxygen in its air manifolds.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Fuel per update = RPS × 4e-6 × listed voxels × fuel throttle, which is RPS × 0.00024 × listed voxels × fuel throttle per simulated second. Intake = RPS × 2.8e-6 × listed voxels ÷ 60 × air throttle × pressure factor, where the pressure factor rises from 1 to 2 with air-manifold pressure (scale 0.01). Efficiency = speed efficiency × mixture factor; speed efficiency = clamp(4(0.02·RPS + 0.5)/(0.02·RPS + 1)² − 1, 0, 1), and the mixture factor 1 − 2(s − 0.6)² peaks at the air:fuel ratio 13.6 cold, 14.0 hot. The displayed Stoichiometric value is 2s − 1, so aim for about 0.2.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The cylinder code multiplies fuel and intake by the definition's listed voxel count: 1 for the 1x1, 27 for the 3x3 and 125 for the 5x5. At equal RPS and throttle a 3x3 cylinder therefore admits 27 times the fuel of a 1x1 and heats its manifolds correspondingly.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: With equal air and fuel throttles and no boost the ratio is 7, below the window, so the engine will not fire; reduce fuel throttle to roughly half of air throttle or add manifold pressure. Exhaust that cannot fit into the exhaust manifolds reduces torque and heat in proportion (Exhaust % in the inspection text). Above 115 °C with overheating enabled the cylinder accumulates damage every 300 updates, once per 5 simulated seconds; while damaged its torque gain halves from 80000 to 40000, and at a counter of 20 it stops producing torque.

sections.title: Open measurement questions
sections.body: Confirm the target ratio in game with the Air:Fuel Ratio inspection line; measure how manifold pressure units relate to the pressure factor; time the damage interval to check the 5-second period.

sections.body: Case 7 runs while the starter input is on and the component is undamaged. It draws electricity through the shared helper and adds speed proportional to (5 − crank RPS), clamped at zero. Its speed is coupled to the crank with weights engine_max_force (0.5) and the crank inertia, then decays by 0.99 per update. Without coupling or drive it would keep 0.547 of its speed after one simulated second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Because assistance ends at 5 RPS and a cylinder needs more than 2 RPS plus a valid mixture, set the throttles before cranking. Large flywheels reduce how fast the starter can bring the crank up.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.
